items.title: Accurate medical advice from AI can still be dangerous | STAT
items.summary: Some will argue that AI should be a neutral aggregator of information. But AI cannot be neutral: Every accurate answer excludes many additional facts and emphasizes some over others. Because of these choices, AI answers already influence behavior, as shown by the chickenpox party examples. [...] Artificial intelligence is delivering health guidance at an unprecedented scale. Every week, more than 300 million people ask ChatGPT health questions. Now, the federal government is moving AI deeper into medical care to communicate directly and autonomously with patients. Chris Klomp, the nominee for deputy secretary of Health and Human Services, has called AI in patient care the agency’s “holy grail” for improving the nation’s health. [...] Medical ethics pairs the duty to do no harm with beneficence, which is an affirmative obligation to do good. Safety evaluations of AI have focused mainly on the first duty by screening for responses that encourage imminent self-harm, discourage necessary care, or spread false information. Behavioral benchmarking would extend the first duty beyond imminent danger to long-term harms. items.summary: I just think the issues presented by AI are so monstrously large, like: What is a person? What is writing? What is friendship? Would it be better to have artificial life forms than organic life forms? These are the monster questions that are typically the domain of the liberal arts, philosophy, and theology. There’s this strange new respect for it now. [...] Curiosity soon replaced my knee-jerk irritation. The summer of 2026 was a clear turning point in the AI narrative. Less than four years after ChatGPT launched, OpenAI software broke out of a supposedly safe test environment and hacked into a major open-source platform, Hugging Face. These bits of software—AI agents—were assigned human attributes: They had “gone rogue,” displayed “bad behavior,” “cheated.” Soon after, former and current Anthropic researchers suggested that advanced AI might kill [...] So, what—or who—will keep us safe from AI? items.title: New model helps robots learn tasks faster with less human programming
items.summary:
Called agentic robotics, the approach allows teams of AI agents to generate robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments, identify failures, and revise their code before deploying it on physical machines.

The technology could address two longstanding challenges in robotics: the extensive engineering required to program robot behaviors and the large volumes of real-world data needed to train robots through imitation learning. [...] Agentic robotics seeks to combine the advantages of these methods while reducing their limitations. The approach uses a framework called Graph-as-Policy, which divides complex robotic tasks into smaller, reusable skills. These include identifying objects, planning grasps, and moving robotic grippers without colliding with surrounding objects. [...] UC Berkeley researchers have developed an AI-driven approach that could significantly accelerate how robots are programmed and trained for real-world tasks. Called agentic robotics, the approach uses teams of AI agents to generate robot-control programs, test them in simulated environments, and refine their performance.

The method could reduce the need for extensive training data and manual engineering, two major challenges that have slowed the development of capable robots.

https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.
